releases.body:
The island takes prompts, and it resizes.

It has a composer at the foot of the drawer now. It names the session the prompt will go to, Enter sends it and steers that session now, and the menu beside it sends it after the current turn ends and shows what is already waiting there.

The session is picked from the tabs you have open in OpenCode, so a session that has ended can be talked to again.

The open drawer can be resized from its bottom and left edges, and it keeps the size it was left at.

And the drawer stays open until you close it. It used to close the moment you clicked away, which is wrong now that it holds a composer: you type a prompt, press Enter, the island gives the keyboard back, and the drawer went with it. The old behaviour is one toggle away in the footer's controls, and it is off by default.

Install: opencode plugin add opencode-island

The plan shows up when the agent calls the tool from inside another one.

The island read the plan from the tool call on the event stream. An agent that calls the island's tool directly was seen, but an agent that calls it from inside another tool was not: the outer tool carries the call in its metadata, and the island was not looking there.

It looks there now. The plan lands either way.

Verified in the running app: the closed bar shows the steps around the one in hand, green for the one done, orange and pulsing on the one in hand, yellow for the one waiting.

The island shows the plan.

The island could show what an agent was doing right now: its orb, its last words, how long it has been going. It could not show the plan, which step of a five step job the agent is on and how much of it is behind it. That is the part a person glancing at the screen edge actually wants.

Under the grip, the steps of the agent's plan: the one before, the one in hand and the one after, each a number and a dot. Green when the step is done, orange and pulsing on the step in hand, yellow for the ones waiting, red for the one that failed. Open the island and every agent shows its whole plan, with a count of how many of its steps are done.

The plan is the agent's own. The plugin gives it one tool, island_plan, and a rule in the global AGENTS.md that asks it to record the steps as it works. The call itself is the record, read off the event stream, so nothing is written to disk inside your project. Delete that block from the global AGENTS.md and the island goes back to showing only the words.

A run that fails takes the step in hand with it, and only that step. A run you stopped, or a tool that failed and the agent recovered from, leaves the plan alone. Another tool's call never takes the plan over, even when the island cannot name the tool.

Verified against a real Electron window: the bar shows the three steps around the one in hand, in order, inside its 36px width, and a plan of twenty steps wraps onto a second line in the open island instead of running over the time.

The bar keeps its length, and counts the agents.

The length of the closed tab was a number that lived in the page, so it was gone the next time OpenCode started. It is kept now, as a share of the screen, and the bar comes back the size you left it.

Under the grip, a number counts the agents that are working, and pops when the count changes.

Verified against a real Electron window: a length of 40 percent came back as 432 pixels after a restart, the resize wrote the share down, and the count animates when it moves from two to three.

The island buttons sit at the foot of the closed tab.

They were floating in the middle of the bar, with a gap above the grip that resizes it, because the words beside them did not fill the space. The bar now leaves that room on purpose: the words take it, the buttons keep the bottom, and the grip stays clear below them.

OpenCode's mark also keeps its own proportions now, instead of being squashed into a square.
